result.title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
result.summary: Generative models trained on the output of earlier models lose knowledge across generations, rare knowledge first. The remedies that work all bring in information from outside the loop, and the theory of model collapse treats that supply as given: a fixed archive, drawn from a fixed distribution. We argue that the supply is the problem, and that cultural evolution has the theory of it. We read model collapse as Rogers' paradox: a population that comes to rely on copying ends up no better off than one that never copied, because copies go stale unless someone keeps learning for themselves. We test the identification in three steps. First, Rogers' model, fitted only to fully synthetic training, predicts to within a few percentage points how much rare knowledge language models, from word trigrams to a pretrained transformer, retain under other mixtures of fresh data. Second, when the world itself changes, a lineage that copies its own past needs more fresh data to keep up the faster the world changes, as Rogers' model says it must and as analyses that assume a fixed target cannot; a lineage that restarts every generation from fixed pretrained weights is largely insulated, because those weights are knowledge that is never copied. Third, we close the loop: when the people who write a model's training data can ask the model instead of finding things out, the supply of fresh data becomes endogenous. At equilibrium, the model is exactly as reliable as it is costly for people to find out for themselves, the population is no better off than without the model, and every increase in the share of model-written text must be paid for by more people learning for themselves. Users who check what they are told and relearn when it is wrong break the paradox. Filters that select plausible text are conformist and accelerate collapse; only checks that carry new information act as critical learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把模型在自身输出上训练所导致的知识退化（稀有知识先丧失）重新表述为文化演化中的 Rogers 悖论，并用 trigram 到预训练 transformer 的合成/混合数据实验与均衡分析论证：关键在于外部新鲜信息的供给，筛选「看似合理」的文本会加速崩溃，只有携带新信息的核查才起纠偏作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「自生成数据逐代丢失稀有信息、唯有引入新信息的校验有效」的论点，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 轨迹自训练与自验证监督的信息坍缩风险。
